## What the data says
- No thin-fabric test runs exist at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa; the predictor reports "NO TEST DATA" for this material class [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- The physics estimate for thin fabric uses n-heptane as a surrogate and gives a target flame temperature ≈2550 K, which is ≈220 K above the hottest thin-fabric microgravity run (≈2320 K) and ≈530 K above the coldest thin-fabric run that still burned (≈2010 K) [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- Droplet tests with methanol at 30-34 % O₂ and 71.2-72.1 kPa show "sustained" burning in all 8 nearest runs (PSI-69); evidence coverage = 0.892, physics margin ≈790 K (physics estimate) [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant materials: 3 of 4 Nomex runs burned and 1 did not (PSI-25, PSI-99); 0 of 4 silicone runs burned (PSI-99). All eight runs were at ≤22.2 % O₂ [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 failure for Nomex HT90-40 at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g is documented (NTRS 20070018178).
- No partial-gravity combustion data exist in PSI; partial gravity may be more hazardous than both micro- and Earth-gravity (NTRS 20260000646).

## How confident we can be
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric is zero because no runs match the target pressure or oxygen level (no test data).
- Solid-material data are limited: 131 of 134 ordinary solid runs were "sustained"; only 2 extinction-velocity limits and 1 no-ignition run exist, preventing a flammability limit determination [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99].
- Droplet evidence is strong (coverage 0.892, 100 % sustained) for methanol at near-target conditions [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant material evidence is sparse (8 runs, mixed outcomes) and confined to ≤22.2 % O₂, so confidence for higher O₂ is low [PSI-25] [PSI-99].

## Gaps
- No thin-fabric microgravity tests at 30 % O₂ or at 70.3 kPa; pressure and oxygen level are outside the tested envelope.
- Solid-material dataset lacks sufficient non-burning runs to locate a flammability limit.
- No fire-resistant material tests at ≥30 % O₂ or at the target pressure.
- No partial-gravity (0.38 g) combustion data; behavior in Martian gravity is untested and may be more hazardous.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric ignition and flame spread at 30 % O₂ and ~70 kPa, with varied flow rates, to provide the first evidence coverage for this class.
- Solid-material runs that intentionally target extinction (low O₂, high flow) to generate measurable non-burning data and define flammability limits.
- Fire-resistant material (silicone, Nomex) tests at ≥30 % O₂ and target pressure to assess behavior beyond the current ≤22.2 % O₂ envelope.
- Partial-gravity combustion experiments (≈0.38 g) for both fabrics and solids to evaluate the hypothesis that flame spread may be more hazardous than in micro- or Earth-gravity.
